answer: Neighborhood Nadir Rule. Each node tracks the connectedness of its transaction neighbors, sampled at a random pulse each epoch; a node whose neighborhood density falls below the rolling nadir is throttled to a fraction of normal routing weight. Freshly spawned identities cluster in sparse, weakly linked regions, so each must sustain costly organic links, at dawn's first epochs especially, before gaining full throughput. An attacker pays per-identity link maintenance and lost capacity at scale, not a one-time fee.
